title: A new multiple of eight from eight thousand five hundred and sixty
description: The thousands are whole eights, the last three digits are seventy eights, and taking away one eight gives eight thousand five hundred and fifty two. Keeko's doubt that fifty two is not a multiple of eight is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the thousands are whole eights and the last three digits decide, so changing the last two digits means moving the last three digits to another multiple of eight. Watch for students who test only the last two digits.

source: Change the last two digits of 8560 so that the resulting number is a multiple of 8.
video_script.why: The child splits the number into thousands and the last three digits, sees that the last three digits are seventy eights, and moves one eight down to get a new multiple.
video_script.substitution: Split off the thousands, count the last three digits in eights, and change them to the neighbouring multiple of eight.
video_script.anchor: the number card 8560 with its last two digits circled, split into 8000 and 560
video_script.wrong_answer: eight thousand five hundred and fifty two is not divisible by eight
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says eight thousand five hundred and fifty two is not divisible by eight, because its last two digits, fifty two, are not a multiple of eight. Five hundred and sixty is seventy eights, so one eight less is sixty nine eights, which is five hundred and fifty two, and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Eight thousand five hundred and fifty two is a multiple of eight

final_answer.spoken: eight thousand five hundred and fifty two is a multiple of eight

maths_rules: 560 = 70 x 8, so 8560 is already divisible by 8
take away one 8: 560 - 8 = 552 = 69 x 8, so the last two digits 60 become 52
other answers also work, for example 8568 = 8 x 1071; the book gives 8552
52 = 6 x 8 + 4 and 500 = 62 x 8 + 4; the two 4s make one more 8, so 552 = 69 x 8
video_script.design: One idea: the thousands are whole eights, the last three digits are counted in eights, and one eight less gives a new multiple. Assumes the test on the last three digits. Wrong idea: the last two digits must themselves be a multiple of eight. The number card stays on the board to the end.

<bookmark mark='name'/>Every number you land on is called a multiple of eight.

beats.on_screen: Given: the number 8560; its last two digits can change

marks.given: the number is written with its last two digits circled

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number eight thousand five hundred and sixty, and we may change its last two digits.

beats.on_screen: To find: a new number, with the same first two digits, that is a multiple of 8
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a new number that is a multiple of eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, split off the thousands: 8560 = 8000 + 560; 8000 = 1000 x 8

marks.split: the number is cut into 8000 and 560
marks.thou: 8000 = 1000 x 8 is written under the first part

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, split the number into eight thousand, and five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>Eight thousand is one thousand eights, so it never leaves anything over.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the last three digits: 560 = 8 x 70

marks.seventy: 560 = 8 x 70 is written and a tick appears
marks.already: the last two digits are circled again

narration: <bookmark mark='seventy'/>Step two, count the last three digits in eights. Eight times seventy is five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='already'/>Eight divides the number already, but we must change the last two digits.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, take away one 8: 560 - 8 = 552 = 8 x 69; the last two digits 60 become 52

marks.away: one group of eight is taken away from the seventy groups
marks.digits: the last two digits change from 60 to 52

narration: <bookmark mark='away'/>Step three, take away one eight. Seventy eights become sixty nine eights.
<bookmark mark='new'/>Five hundred and sixty less eight is five hundred and fifty two.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>The last two digits change from sixty to fifty two.

marks.add: the thousand eights and the sixty nine eights are added to 1069 eights
marks.check: 8 x 1069 = 8552 is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, check the new number. One thousand eights and sixty nine eights make one thousand and sixty nine eights.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Eight times one thousand and sixty nine is eight thousand five hundred and fifty two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Eight thousand five hundred and fifty two is a multiple of eight.
Its last two digits are fifty two, and the last three digits are sixty nine eights.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble pointing at the last two digits 52; 560 = 70 eights; one eight less is 69 eights = 552; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble appears and points at the last two digits 52 of 8552
marks.sixty: 560 = 70 eights is shown with one eight taken away

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eight thousand five hundred and fifty two is not divisible by eight.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The reason is that its last two digits, fifty two, are not a multiple of eight.
<bookmark mark='sixty'/>But five hundred and sixty is seventy eights. One eight less is sixty nine eights, which is five hundred and fifty two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The last three digits decide, so we do not test the last two alone.
